imagining that, if we grant that divine existence for which you so earnestly contend, you may
safely infer consequences from it and add something to the experienced order of nature
by arguing from the attributes which you ascribe to your gods. You seem not to remember that
all your reasonings on this subject can only be drawn from effects to causes, and that

it is impossible for you to know anything of the cause, but what you have antecedently,
not inferred, but discovered to the full in the effect.
